neighbours.label: the sentence-closing punctuation of a heartfelt first-person statement (a prayer, a vow, a confession, a tired remark in dialogue), as against the same punctuation closing neutral third-person reports
fire: I lift my eyes to the Lord, who is my strength and my song.
I swear to stand beside you for the rest of my days.
I have made so many mistakes, and I am truly sorry.
She rubbed her eyes and said, "I'm worn out. Let's call it a night."
I will praise You, O God, with all my heart.
I give you my word that I will never leave you.
I am a sinner, and I have no one to turn to but You.
He sighed. "I'm done. I can't do this anymore."
quiet: The council approved the new parking rules on Monday.
The bridge was closed for repairs for most of the year.
The company reported higher profits in the third quarter.
The train left the station twenty minutes late.
The museum will reopen after the renovation in spring.
The report lists the costs of each project in detail.
The river rose by two metres after the heavy rain.
The school added three new classrooms last summer.

predictions: fire 0.3-0.7 on the final '.' or ',' of first-person vows, prayers and confessions; neutral third-person reports below 0.15
short: close of a heartfelt first-person statement
